item.title: Observing Intimacies: System-Theoretical Analyses of Love Relationships Today
item.content:encoded:
Intimate relationships have undergone significant transformations globally, with relationship ideals and forms becoming increasingly diverse across commitment types, duration, and organization. This special issue aims to advance knowledge production by promoting observational rather than normative approaches to intimacies, encouraging data-driven scholarship that moves beyond polarized public debates about relationships.

The issue revitalizes Luhmann's systems theory approach to intimate relationships and love as communication media in modern societies. It invites scholars to apply systems-theoretical concepts to examine contemporary transformations of intimate life across different sociocultural contexts, bridging gaps between geographically or culturally isolated scholarly conversations.

Contributions may adopt two perspectives: analyzing intimate systems through systems theory concepts and examining how other social systems (law, politics, media, education) observe and shape intimacies. The special issue welcomes diverse empirical work grounded in theoretical frameworks, particularly from varied sociocultural environments.

Appel publié par Kybernetes. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Social systems theory
  • Sociology of intimacy
  • Sexualities
  • Gender
  • Social semantics
  • Applications of Luhmann's systems theory to intimate relationships
  • Semantic and social evolution of intimate relationships
  • Programs and semantic repertoires for intimacy across historical and cultural contexts
  • Intimacy reproduction through self-reference and communicative improbability
  • Platforms, markets, and mobilities reconfiguring intimate communication
  • Expectations stabilization under volatility and dealing with disappointment
  • Legal categories and their observation of intimate possibilities
  • Media and platform logics observing relationship norms
  • Moral and political discourses on specific intimacies
  • Political mobilization of intimacy and family values
  • Queer intimacies and inclusion/exclusion effects
